223d79e8-1f2c-407a-8c98-9a4e931f8b1f.title: Add Jira search/read capability with settings-driven configuration
223d79e8-1f2c-407a-8c98-9a4e931f8b1f.details:
## Goal Give Echo agents the ability to query a configured Jira instance so they can evaluate current tasks, bugs, and work items relevant to what they're doing. ## Design — One Tool, Not Three A single `jira_search` tool that accepts a JQL query string. The model generates the right JQL on its own: - `key = PROJ-123` → single ticket read (replaces Jane's `jira_ticket_read`) - `assignee = currentUser() AND status IN ("To Do", "In Progress")` → user's current tasks - `project = ECHO AND type = Bug AND priority >= High ORDER BY created DESC` → filtered search This is the same approach as Jane's `jira_search`, just unified. The model already constructs complex strings for `web_search.query`, `shell_command.command`, and `git_inspect`. No problem forming a JQL string. ## Settings — Token in UI, Not Hardcoded Add 3 fields to `llm.Settings` (not env vars like Jane): ```go JiraURL string `json:"jiraUrl"` // e.g. https://company.atlassian.net or self-hosted URL JiraUsername string `json:"jiraUsername"` // Email for Cloud, username for Server JiraAPIToken string `json:"jiraApiToken"` // API token from Atlassian account / PAT for Server ``` - Empty `JiraURL` = disabled (like ComfyUI pattern) - Validate as HTTP/HTTPS URL in `Settings.Validate()` - Normalize/trim in `Settings.normalized()` - Clone in `Settings.Clone()` (token is a plain string, no special handling needed — it persists to `state.json` like all settings) ## Frontend Settings UI Add a **"Jira"** section in `frontend/src/app/settings/index.ts`, after the Search section: ```html

Jira

Configure your Jira instance so agents can query issues and evaluate current tasks.

Base URL of your Jira Cloud or self-hosted instance. Leave empty to disable.

For Jira Cloud, create an API token at id.atlassian.com/manage/security/api-tokens. For self-hosted Jira Server, use a personal access token.

``` No additional save logic needed — the form serialization maps `name=` attributes to `llm.Settings` fields via JSON tags automatically (existing pattern). ## New Files ### `internal/jira/client.go` — HTTP client Adapted from Jane's `ext_services/atlassian/jira/jira_api/jira_jql.go`: ```go package jira type Client struct { baseURL string // e.g. https://company.atlassian.net username string apiToken string httpClient *http.Client } func New(baseURL, username, apiToken string) (*Client, error) { // Strip trailing slash from baseURL, validate it's HTTP/HTTPS // Error if baseURL is empty } func (c *Client) Search(ctx context.Context, jql string, fields []string, maxResults int) (*SearchResponse, error) { // GET /rest/api/3/search?jql={encoded}&fields={comma-joined}&maxResults=N&startAt=offset // Auto-paginate if results exceed maxResults (Jane does this) // Auth: Basic(base64(username + ":" + apiToken)) for Cloud // Or Bearer token — try Basic first, fall back to Bearer } // Helper: convert Jira's ADF (Atlassian Document Format) nested JSON to plain text. // Jane does this in jira_jql.go:extractADFNodeText() — copy the logic directly. func adfToText(node ADFNode) string { ... } ``` Key behaviors from Jane to replicate: - **Auto-pagination**: Jira caps at 50/100 results per page. Loop with `startAt` until `total - startAt <= maxResults`. Cap total loop iterations to avoid runaway (max ~10 pages = 1000 issues). - **ADF text extraction**: Jane converts Atlassian's nested document format (`doc → paragraph → text`) into readable plain text for descriptions and comments. Copy the switch/case logic from `jira_jql.go:extractADFNodeText()`. - **Field minimization**: Jane strips `self`, `expand`, avatar URLs, etc. via `MinimalJson()` to save tokens. Do similar pruning in Echo's types. ### `internal/jira/types.go` — Response types Copy Jane's types from `jira_jql.go` directly: ```go type SearchResponse struct { Expand string `json:"expand"` StartAt int `json:"startAt"` MaxResults int `json:"maxResults"` Total int `json:"total"` Issues []Ticket `json:"issues"` } type Ticket struct { Expand string `json:"expand"` ID string `json:"id"` Key string `json:"key"` Self string `json:"self"` Fields TicketFields `json:"fields"` } type TicketFields struct { Summary string `json:"summary"` Description ADFNode `json:"description"` DescriptionText string `json:"descriptionText,omitempty"` // populated by client Status TicketStatus `json:"status"` Priority TicketPriority `json:"priority"` Assignee TicketAccount `json:"assignee"` Creator TicketAccount `json:"creator"` Created string `json:"created"` Updated string `json:"updated"` Components []TicketComponent `json:"components"` Labels []string `json:"labels"` Comment TicketComments `json:"comment"` Issuelinks []LinkedTicket `json:"issuelinks"` IssueType TicketType `json:"issuetype"` // add this from Jane's missing field } // ADFNode, ADFMark — for ADF text conversion (from Jane) // TicketComments, TicketComment — comment container // TicketAccount, AvatarUrls — user info (prune avatars/self in output) // TicketPriority, TicketStatus, TicketComponent, LinkedTicket, TicketType ``` ### `internal/jira/client_test.go` — Tests Use `httptest.Server` with mock Jira JSON responses: - Successful search with multiple pages (verifies pagination) - Single ticket via `key = PROJ-123` query - Empty results - Auth failure (401) - ADF → text conversion on description and comments - Connection error ### `internal/tools/jira.go` — Tool registration ```go func init() { Register(ToolFunc{ Meta: Metadata{ Name: "jira_search", Description: `Search Jira for issues using a JQL (Jira Query Language) query. Use key = PROJ-123 to read a single issue, assignee = currentUser() AND status IN ("To Do", "In Progress") for your current tasks, or any valid JQL expression.`, Parameters: Schema{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": []any{"query"}, "properties": map[string]any{ "query": map[string]any{ "type": "string", "description": "JQL query string. Examples: key = PROJ-123, assignee = currentUser(), project = ECHO AND status != Done.", }, "maxResults": map[string]any{ "type": "integer", "description": "Maximum issues to return. Defaults to 10, max 50.", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 50, }, "fields": map[string]any{ "type": "array", "items": map[string]any{"type": "string"}, "description": "Fields to include. If omitted, returns key, summary, status, priority, assignee, type, labels, created, updated, description, components.", }, }, }, }, Run: jiraSearch, }) } type jiraArgs struct { Query string `json:"query"` MaxResults int `json:"maxResults"` Fields []string `json:"fields,omitempty"` } type jiraResult struct { Query string `json:"query"` Total int `json:"total"` Returned int `json:"returned"` Issues []jiraIssue `json:"issues"` } type jiraIssue struct { Key string `json:"key"` Summary string `json:"summary"` Status string `json:"status"` Priority string `json:"priority"` Type string `json:"type"` Assignee string `json:"assignee,omitempty"` Labels []string `json:"labels,omitempty"` Created string `json:"created,omitempty"` Updated string `json:"updated,omitempty"` Description string `json:"description,omitempty"` // plain text from ADF Comments []jiraComment `json:"comments,omitempty"` } type jiraComment struct { Author string `json:"author"` Body string `json:"body"` // plain text from ADF Created string `json:"created"` } ``` In `jiraSearch`: 1. Parse args, validate query is non-empty 2. If `ctx.JiraURL` is empty → return `SafeError{Code: "not_configured", Message: "Jira is not configured. Set Jira Base URL in settings."}` 3. Create client with `jira.New(ctx.JiraURL, ctx.JiraUsername, ctx.JiraAPIToken)` 4. Default fields if omitted: `"summary,status,priority,assignee,description,comment,type,labels,components"` (matches Jane's `DefaultFields`) 5. Call `client.Search()`, then marshal results into flat `jiraResult` struct (not raw JSON — Echo pattern) 6. Strip `self`, `avatarUrls`, `accountId`, etc. from accounts (Jane does this in `MinimalJson()`) ### `internal/tools/jira_test.go` - Unconfigured Jira returns `not_configured` error - Empty query returns `invalid_arguments` - Successful search with mock client (use an interface for the client to inject mock) - Cancellation propagates via context ## Wiring Changes ### `internal/llm/settings.go` - Add `JiraURL`, `JiraUsername`, `JiraAPIToken` fields to `Settings` struct - Trim in `normalized()` — only `JiraURL` needs URL validation if non-empty - Validate `JiraURL` as HTTP/HTTPS in `Validate()` (only if non-empty) - Copy in `Clone()` ### `internal/tools/types.go` Add to `ExecutionContext`: ```go JiraURL string JiraUsername string JiraAPIToken string ``` ### Wire ExecutionContext — search and update all `ExecutionContext{...}` instantiations: **`internal/services/chat.go`** — In `sendChatMessage`, wherever `tools.ExecutionContext{..., SearxngURL: settings.SearxngURL, ...}` is built, add the 3 Jira fields. **`internal/services/chat_research.go`** — Same pattern for research agent execution contexts. **`internal/services/file_changes.go`** — Same if tools are wired there. **`internal/services/kanban_scheduler.go`** — If kanban agents use tools, same pattern. Search for `SearxngURL:` in `internal/services/` to find all ExecutionContext construction sites. ### `internal/tools/registry.go` Add `"jira_search"` to `readOnlyToolNames` so it's available in plan/research modes. ## Verification ```powershell go test ./... cd frontend; npm run build; cd .. wails dev # verify settings section appears, tool shows in schema ``` ## Key Behaviors to Preserve from Jane 1. **ADF text extraction** — Jira stores descriptions/comments as nested Atlassian Document Format JSON. Jane converts this recursively (`doc → paragraph → text → "text"`). Without this conversion, the agent gets unusable raw ADF blobs. Copy the `extractADFNodeText` logic exactly. 2. **Auto-pagination** — Jira API returns max 50-100 results per call. Loop with `startAt` until done or hit a page cap (~10 pages / ~1000 issues max). 3. **Token minimization** — Strip URL-only fields (`self`, avatar URLs, `accountId`, etc.) from the output to avoid wasting context tokens on useless data. 4. **Field selection** — Default field list should include everything useful for task evaluation: key, summary, description, status, priority, assignee, type, labels, components, comment, created, updated. ## Key Differences from Jane | Aspect | Jane | Echo | |---|---|---| | Auth source | `ATLASSIAN_AUTH_TOKEN` env var | Settings UI → `state.json` | | Base URL | Hardcoded in config | User-configured per instance | | Project key | Hardcoded (`NF`) | Model specifies via JQL | | Tool split | Separate search + ticket read | One unified tool | | Output format | Raw JSON string / CSV table | Structured Go type → JSON marshaled by tool system | | Auth method | Bearer token only | Basic auth (username:API-token) for Cloud, works for Server too |
acceptanceCriteria: Settings fields JiraURL, JiraUsername, JiraAPIToken exist in llm.Settings with validation and normalization
Frontend settings UI has a Jira section with base URL, username, and API token inputs
Jira client handles HTTP auth, pagination, and ADF-to-text conversion
jira_search tool accepts JQL query and optional maxResults/fields parameters
ExecutionContext passes Jira config from settings through to tools
Tool returns clear 'not configured' error when JiraURL is empty
jira_search is in readOnlyToolNames for plan/research mode availability
Go tests cover client pagination, ADF conversion, auth errors, and tool argument validation
Frontend builds without errors; go test ./... passes

6fee9d83-f2bc-4bfb-a9d6-274577541c6c.title: Terminal saved commands with CRUD
6fee9d83-f2bc-4bfb-a9d6-274577541c6c.details:
## Terminal Saved Commands — Implementation Plan ### Backend (Go) **`internal/services/system.go`** - Add type: ```go type SavedCommand struct { ID string `json:"id"` Name string `json:"name"` Command string `json:"command"` Order int `json:"order"` } ``` - Add to `AppState`: `SavedCommands map[string][]SavedCommand \`json:"savedCommands,omitempty"\`` - Add methods: - `GetSavedCommands(workspaceID string) []SavedCommand` — validate workspace, return deep clone - `UpsertSavedCommand(workspaceID, id, name, command string, order int) error` — create if id empty (UUID), update if exists; trim+validate inputs; clone slice before mutation; save - `DeleteSavedCommand(workspaceID, id string) error` — filter out matching id from workspace's slice; save **`internal/services/state_persistence.go`** - Update `cloneStateLocked` to deep-copy `SavedCommands` map **`internal/webserver/server.go`** - Add `"GetSavedCommands"`, `"UpsertSavedCommand"`, `"DeleteSavedCommand"` to RPC whitelist ### Regenerate bindings - Run `wails generate` ### Frontend Types **`frontend/src/app/types.ts`** ```ts export type SavedCommand = { id: string; name: string; command: string; order: number; }; ``` ### Frontend State **`frontend/src/app/state.ts`** - Add to state object: - `savedCommands: new Map()` - `savedCommandEditingId: ""` - `savedCommandDraftName: ""` - `savedCommandDraftCommand: ""` ### Frontend Backend Services **`frontend/src/backend/services.ts`** - Add: ```ts export async function GetSavedCommands(workspaceID: string): Promise { ... } export async function UpsertSavedCommand(workspaceID, id, name, command: string, order: number): Promise { ... } export async function DeleteSavedCommand(workspaceID, id: string): Promise { ... } ``` ### Frontend Render **`frontend/src/app/render.ts`** In `renderTerminalPanel`, insert between `.terminal-runs` and `.terminal-input-row`: ```html
${icons.bookmark} Saved Commands
``` Each saved command row: - Command text (clickable to run) - Edit button (✎) → switches to inline form - Delete button (✕) Inline edit form: name input + command textarea + Save/Cancel buttons. ### Frontend Actions **`frontend/src/app/actions.ts`** - `run-saved-command`: Get from saved list, set terminalDrafts, trigger run-shell-command - `add-saved-command`: Read current terminal input; if non-empty generate UUID and call UpsertSavedCommand with name = truncated command or "Untitled" - `edit-saved-command`: Set editing state for that id, populate draft fields, re-render - `delete-saved-command`: Call backend DeleteSavedCommand, re-render - `save-edited-command`: Validate inputs, call UpsertSavedCommand with existing id, clear edit state, re-render ### Frontend Patch Support **`frontend/src/app/bootstrap.ts`** - In `patchTerminalPanel`, also patch `[data-terminal-saved-list]` innerHTML so saved-command changes don't require full re-render. ### CSS **`frontend/src/styles.css`** ```css .terminal-saved-commands { /* collapsible section */ } .terminal-saved-header summary { /* styled like terminal header */ } .terminal-saved-list { /* scrollable list */ } .terminal-saved-item { /* flex row: command text + action buttons */ } .terminal-saved-run { /* main clickable area */ } .terminal-saved-edit, .terminal-saved-delete { /* small icon buttons */ } .terminal-add-saved { /* compact add button */ } /* Inline edit form styles */ /* Mobile tap target: min 36px height on interactive elements */ ``` ### Bootstrap Load **`frontend/src/app/bootstrap.ts`** - After `LoadState`, call `GetSavedCommands` for each workspace and populate `state.savedCommands`. ### Verification - Desktop: wails dev, verify saved commands appear in terminal panel - Mobile/web: verify tap targets are usable - Persistence: restart app, verify saved commands persist - `go test ./...` - `cd frontend; npm run build`

New package with HTTP client for the Jira REST API v3:

f1b4a109-2674-4971-a964-2b688f090754.title: Fix saved command dialog obscured by bottom nav on mobile
f1b4a109-2674-4971-a964-2b688f090754.details:
## Problem
On mobile (≤720px), the Save/Cancel buttons in the saved command dialog (.saved-command-dialog) can be hidden behind the fixed bottom navigation bar (.mobile-bottom-nav).

## Root Cause
The dialog overlay uses `place-items: center` for vertical centering, which doesn't account for the ~64px fixed bottom nav. No max-height constraint exists on mobile (unlike Kanban modals which were previously fixed).

## Change
**File:** `echo/frontend/src/styles.css` — inside existing `@media (max-width: 720px)` block (~line 9606):

Add to `.saved-command-dialog`:
- `max-height: calc(100vh - 96px);` — leaves breathing room above the bottom nav
- `overflow-y: auto;` — scrolls content if dialog exceeds max-height

This mirrors the existing pattern for Kanban modals (.card-detail, .kanban-card-create-dialog) which use the same constraint in this breakpoint.

## Verification
- `cd frontend; npm run build` — TypeScript/Vite build passes
- Manual: on mobile viewport (≤720px), open terminal → click "Save current" → Save/Cancel buttons should be visible above the bottom nav bar

fb940a9c-0e45-4f02-ad37-0cb695fc0bb7.title: Enforce mandatory Kanban fields on backlog task creation
fb940a9c-0e45-4f02-ad37-0cb695fc0bb7.details:
## Problem

When an agent creates a backlog task (via `workspace_task_create`), it often omits the fields that `CreateReadyKanbanCard` requires. Later, when the user tries to create a Kanban card from that task — either via the "Create Kanban Card" button in the UI or through `CreateReadyKanbanCard(workspaceID, title, description, acceptanceCriteria)` — the call is rejected with errors like:

- `"description is required"`
- `"at least one acceptance criterion is required"`

This forces the user to fill in the missing fields manually instead of the agent doing it upfront.

## Requirement

Every future backlog task created via `workspace_task_create` MUST include all three Kanban-card-required fields:

1. **`title`** — concise imperative phrase (already a required parameter)
2. **`details`** — concrete implementation description, not just one-liners; must be non-empty after trim
3. **`acceptanceCriteria`** — at least one observable, verifiable acceptance criterion array entry

If any of these are missing or effectively empty on task creation, the agent should treat it as incomplete and refine the task rather than leaving a half-baked backlog item.

## Validation reference

The backend validation in `internal/services/kanban.go:CreateReadyKanbanCard` rejects cards when:
- `title == ""` (after trim)
- `description == ""` (after trim)
- `acceptanceCriteria` has zero non-empty entries after trimming each element

The agent prompt or system instructions should mirror these same rules at the point of `workspace_task_create` so that every task in `.echo/backlog.md` is immediately convertible to a Kanban card without user intervention.

## Scope

This applies to:
- Agent-created tasks (primary target — the decomposer/agent calling `workspace_task_create`)
- It may also inform prompt updates in `internal/services/decomposition.go` or workspace skill notes to reinforce the rule at creation time, not just at conversion time.
acceptanceCriteria: New backlog tasks created via workspace_task_create include non-empty title, details (description), and at least one acceptance criterion
The agent refuses to create a task if any of the three required Kanban fields are missing or effectively empty after trimming
An existing backlog task with missing fields can be retroactively updated to include all three before creating a Kanban card from it
The rejection errors from CreateReadyKanbanCard (title is required, description is required, at least one acceptance criterion is required) are prevented by enforcement at task-creation time
